name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: From Reactive Containment to Proactive Assurance: Lessons from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Agent Security Incidents
items.dek: Agent eval escapes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) show boundaries fail under test; proposes Boundary Assurance Stack for runtime verification.
items.unproven: Framework not yet deployed in live agent systems; cases are post-hoc analysis, not prospective validation of the PASAC model.

items.title: Provable Subexponential Algorithms for NIST Third-Round Lattice Families
items.dek: Subexponential lattice algorithms break Kyber, FrodoKEM, SABER, NTRU, and Dilithium with polylogarithmic coefficient scales; initiate migration planning immediately.
items.unproven: whether NIST parameter choices fall within vulnerable regime; classical-only, no quantum speedup analysis; migration timeline and cryptanalytic feasibility against deployed hardened implementations unclear.

items.title: Skill Constellations: Tracing the Supply Chain of Agent Skills on GitHub
items.dek: 14.9% of high-risk agent skill adoptions prevented by auditing top-100 source repositories ranked by copy network, versus 0.5% for most-starred.
items.unproven: whether ranking generalizes as new skills enter ecosystem; limited to GitSkills dataset; assumes reader has visibility into SKILL.md supply chain in current SDLC.

items.title: I think we might lose public key cryptography
items.dek: Post-quantum cryptography timeline concerns; informs migration planning but offers no new technical findings.
items.unproven: no quantified threat calendar or migration path beyond speculation

items.title: HPQ-AKE: A Provably Secure Sign-Less Hybrid Authenticated Key Exchange Protocol for Bandwidth-Constrained IoT and Edge Networks
items.dek: HPQ-AKE replaces post-quantum signatures with dual KEMs for IoT handshakes; reduces bandwidth 57%, proven secure in extended BR model.
items.unproven: Analytical model and simulation only; no hardware or firmware deployment data; RSA infrastructure assumption may not hold for all IoT gateways; reader's org likely preparing PQC migration planning, but implementation is GRC-level, not SDLC-integrated.

items.title: From Public Posts to AI-Search Citations: Measuring the Fragility of AI Search
items.dek: Measurement framework reveals low-barrier publication domains can become indirect citation paths into AI-search answers across 10 platforms.
items.unproven: attack feasibility and real-world exploitation likelihood; whether platforms adjust citation selection post-disclosure.

items.title: A Security Meta-Model for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
items.dek: Security meta-model maps attack surfaces, weaknesses, and CIA impacts for RAG systems with interactive risk profiling by deployment type.
items.unproven: whether the 43-paper taxonomy achieves sufficient coverage for novel RAG architectures entering production; validation against real deployments.

items.title: Where Do the Tokens Go? Understanding and Reducing Costs in LLM Agents for Vulnerability Discovery
items.dek: Study of 200 LLM agent runs reveals code localization and vulnerability reasoning consume 60.4% of tokens in failed vulnerability discovery.
items.unproven: whether AVRI improvements generalize beyond CyberGym or to agents with different architectures; reproducibility across different LLM models and versions.

items.title: Stop My Dancing! Understanding, Detecting and Attributing Motion-Aware Deepfake Videos
items.dek: First motion-aware deepfake benchmark and detector exploiting synthesis artifacts at motion boundaries; 94.8% in-distribution accuracy.
items.unproven: Cross-dataset accuracy drops to 89.1%; does not address adaptive adversary or video compression beyond tested codecs; six generators only.

items.title: Telegram Desktop vulnerability allowed any user's file to be stolen
items.dek: Telegram Desktop path traversal allowed file theft; vulnerability now patched.
items.unproven: whether the flaw affected production deployments at scale or only under specific user conditions

items.title: Entanglement entropy and magic of ZX-diagrams
items.dek: ZX-diagram graphical rewriting enables efficient estimation of entanglement and magic without tensor contraction.
items.unproven: scalability beyond benchmarked circuit families; practical utility for quantum circuit design workflows

items.title: Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits
items.dek: Virtual error cancellation mitigates logical quantum errors from syndrome records alone, bypassing noise characterization.
items.unproven: demonstration on hardware beyond simulation; fault-tolerant regime scalability; practical decoder latency requirements

items.title: Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection
items.dek: Breaks one-half barrier for Shamir secret-sharing local leakage resilience; advances polynomial intersection bounds.
items.unproven: Pure cryptography theory; no systems deployment or migration path to real-world secret-sharing infrastructure.

items.title: Quantum Co-Design of Inhomogeneous Many-Body Neutrino Fast Flavor Transformation
items.dek: Quantum co-design simulates inhomogeneous neutrino flavor evolution with TEBD circuits and resource estimates through N=50.
items.unproven: entirely outside application security engineer's remit

items.title: ReSI: Recursive Safety Improvement toward Resistant and Resilient AI
items.dek: ReSI framework automates recursive safety improvement through red-teaming and Pareto-gated updates; terminology of resistance and resilience.
items.unproven: No deployment data; unclear whether recursive self-improvement via automated research is safer than supervised human review; agent safety is entering SDLC but this is still research-stage.

items.title: Autonomous Code Migration for Quantum Programming Languages: A Case Study with QED-C Benchmarks
items.dek: LLM agents successfully port 13 quantum benchmarks from Qiskit to CUDA-Q with minimal human intervention.
items.unproven: single domain (quantum frameworks); no evidence this generalizes to mixed classical-quantum SDLC; agents used shortcuts and required re-prompting

items.title: Poster: A Preliminary Study of LLM Distillation Inference
items.dek: Hypothesis test using shadow models detects LLM distillation attacks; TPR 1.0 at significance 0.02 on Qwen-to-Llama pair.
items.unproven: Single teacher-student pair tested; no evidence method generalizes across model families, sizes, or training regimes; detection only, no prevention or integration into SDLC.

items.title: Could LLM Watermark Detection be Public?
items.dek: Public LLM watermark detection poses limited new risk; proposes split-key method to enable detection while preserving forensics.
items.unproven: Watermarking is a post-deployment trace mechanism; reader does not own chatbot or agent watermarking; no evidence of integration with SAST/DAST/SCA or SDLC controls.

items.title: Protecting CPU AI On Edge TEEs: WebAssembly's Promise and Practical Challenges
items.dek: WebAssembly in OP-TEE protects edge AI model IP from root; 22% overhead vs hand-ported TEE code, 6% inference latency.
items.unproven: Edge deployment pattern; reader focuses on SDLC and architecture for mid-size financial services, not edge hardware deployment; no evidence integration into model supply chain or build pipeline.

items.title: Anytime-valid detection of LLM weight exfiltration
items.dek: Sequential e-process detects weight exfiltration via token encoding by combining weak evidence across prompts with anytime false-alarm control.
items.unproven: detection latency acceptable for operational response; calibration transfer assumption holds across model families and inference serving deployments; adversary cannot evade by encoding fewer bits.

items.title: Beyond QAOA: A Review of AI and Quantum Computing for Adaptive Combinatorial Optimization
items.dek: Survey of 119 papers on AI-assisted quantum optimization finds stronger evidence for AI improving quantum than reverse.
items.unproven: limited to simulation; no deployed quantum systems measured; evidence for quantum-to-AI direction remains small-scale

items.title: Parameter-Dependent Noise Resilience in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
items.dek: QAOA stability under Pauli noise depends on variational parameters; derives bounds and mitigation strategies.
items.unproven: theoretical bounds and simulated noise; no deployed hardware validation; applicability to production quantum processors unclear

items.title: Error-Corrected Memory and Logic on a Heavy-Hex Superconducting-Qubit Processor
items.dek: Error-corrected quantum memory on 156-qubit superconducting processor improves logical error rates 35–56% with noise-aware decoding.
items.unproven: single hardware implementation on one processor architecture; scalability to larger codes and different fabrication runs undemonstrated; no production deployment

items.title: LTBD: Learnable Trust-Boundary Delimiters for Prompt Injection Defense
items.dek: Learnable delimiters encode trust boundaries in prompts without model fine-tuning, achieving near-zero attack success on benchmarks.
items.unproven: robustness against adaptive attacks specifically targeting delimiter tokens; generalization beyond AlpacaFarm and TaskTracker; deployment cost and compatibility with production LLM inference pipelines.

items.title: A Zero-Knowledge Signature Framework for Efficient Post-Quantum Message Authentication in Cooperative Automated Driving
items.dek: Zero-knowledge signature framework compresses post-quantum V2X authentication overhead; backward compatible with ECDSA.
items.unproven: Simulation only on liboqs and Bulletproofs libraries; no vehicle hardware testing, no actual CAM latency or throughput validation against IEEE 1609.2 requirements.

noise.title: `123456' password used in Danish CPR data breach
noise.dek: Danish breach exposed millions; attackers used trivial password on admin account.

noise.title: Germany transforms former coal mines into Europe's largest lake landscape
noise.dek: Germany converts mines to lakes; environmental infrastructure project unrelated to security.

noise.title: Scam American companies are using to manipulate ingredient lists
noise.dek: Social media thread on ingredient list manipulation; consumer fraud, not software security.
